Water Users Day Use Area (Lower Salt).operator: USDA Forest Service (Tonto NF, Mesa Ranger District)
Water Users Day Use Area (Lower Salt).sourceName: Access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Water Users Day Use Area (Site Open). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking (owner-supplied), checked on Esri World Imagery
Water Users Day Use Area (Lower Salt).note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate is owner-supplied (North's own Google Maps satellite marking, 33.5541561, -111.5433992) and checked on Esri World Imagery z19 on 2026-10-26 (research/raw/imagery/water_users_day_use_area_lower_salt_owner_z19.png); it is NOT an agency coordinate. On imagery: North's point sits on the open sand clearing where the foot paths from the day-use parking lot reach the north bank, about 10-20 m from the channel edge across a bare silt/gravel bar; no constructed ramp (natural shore launch). The USFS EDW point (recareaid 35407) is in the paved lot about 156 m north. The waterline moves with Stewart Mountain Dam releases. NHD High Resolution flowline 37 m away. Superseded agency point: USFS EDW Recreation Opportunities, recareaid 35407 'Water Users Day Use Area' (same coordinate on the Tonto NF page) at 33.555518, -111.543833 (https://apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW/EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01/MapServer/0/query?where=recareaid%3D35407&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=json). Legal boating access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Water Users Day Use Area (Site Open) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/recreation/water-users-day-use-area): 'Water Users is a popular site for kayakers and tubers.' 'This site is most popular as a launch site' 'Motorized boats are not allowed to launch at this site.' Tonto Daily Pass (and Watercraft Sticker, if required). Spot-check this point first; imagery date is not published by Esri.

Blue Point Day Use Area (Lower Salt).note: Research-only grade: access-verified (official source names boating access; approximate area only). Imagery: the point is in the day-use parking lot about 110 m east of the river channel. v1.3: North's owner-supplied point (33.5539720, -111.5750868) is at the water's edge on the beach just south of the Bush Highway bridge (NHD 49 m, river right), but that beach is on the Pebble Beach side of the highway (175 m from the Pebble Beach page coordinate, 193 m from the Blue Point one), so it was not applied. v1.4: reassessed with North's statement that Sheeps Crossing is the other side (his Sheeps point is river-left, 432 m away) and the USFS INFRA site points (Pebble Beach 95705 serves the south lots; Blue Point 95316 is the lot north of the highway); still not applied (research/replacement-proposals-AZ.json). Official source names boating access, but the exact water-entry point is not pinned by an agency coordinate confirmed on imagery.

Goldfield Day Use Area (Lower Salt).note: Research-only grade: access-verified (official source names boating access; approximate area only). Agency point is 257 m from the NHD centreline (>150 m). Tonto order 03-12-03-24-65 closes a described Goldfield-area eagle zone Dec 1-Jun 30 each year (order text runs to Jun 30, 2026; renewal for 2026-27 not found this pass).

Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Lower Salt).operator: USDA Forest Service (Tonto NF, Mesa Ranger District)
Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Lower Salt).sourceName: Access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Site Open). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking (owner-supplied), checked on Esri World Imagery
Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Lower Salt).note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate is owner-supplied (North's own Google Maps satellite marking, 33.5465461, -111.6616464) and checked on Esri World Imagery z19 on 2026-10-26 (research/raw/imagery/phon_d_sutton_day_use_area_lower_salt_owner_z19.png); it is NOT an agency coordinate. On imagery: North's point sits at the waterline on the south bank of the Salt, on an open sandy/rocky shore reached by foot paths from the western Phon D Sutton parking lots and ramadas, just below the Verde River confluence (the Verde enters from the north opposite). No constructed ramp (natural shore take-out). The Tonto NF page point (EDW recareaid 35397) is in the eastern parking lot about 420 m east (60 m south of the river there); the paved site road links both lot groups, and EDW lists no other recreation site between Raccoon Bluff (1.7 km upstream) and this point. The waterline moves with Salt and Verde dam releases. NHD High Resolution flowline 17 m away. Superseded agency point: Tonto NF Phon D Sutton page coordinate (USFS EDW Recreation Opportunities recareaid 35397 'Phon D Sutton Day Use Area': 33.547016, -111.657843) at 33.54697106, -111.6571505 (https://apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW/EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01/MapServer/0/query?where=recareaid%3D35397&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=json). Legal boating access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Site Open) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/recreation/phon-d-sutton-day-use-area): 'This site is a popular inner tube take-out point.' Tonto Daily Pass (and Watercraft Sticker, if required). Spot-check this point first; imagery date is not published by Esri.
Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Lower Salt).bankSourceName: USGS NHD High Resolution flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Lower Salt).bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~250), the point is left of the NHD centreline (17 m). Imagery agrees: the point, the parking lots and the site road are on the south bank (river left when facing downstream, flow to the west-southwest).

Beasley Flat (Verde).operator: USDA Forest Service (Prescott NF, Verde RD)
Beasley Flat (Verde).sourceName: Access: USDA Forest Service, Prescott NF: Beasley Flat Picnic Site; AZ State Parks Paddle Map 2 (Mile 0.0). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking (owner-supplied), checked on Esri World Imagery
Beasley Flat (Verde).note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate is owner-supplied (North's own Google Maps satellite marking, 34.4734529, -111.8012007) and checked on Esri World Imagery z19 on 2026-10-26 (research/raw/imagery/beasley_flat_verde_owner_z19.png); it is NOT an agency coordinate. On imagery: North's point sits in a bare sandy clearing that runs through a gap in the west-bank riparian trees to open water, about 8 m from the waterline, directly east of the paved Beasley Flat picnic loop. The concrete ramp surface the paddle guide describes is not clearly distinguishable on the imagery, but this is the only open shore gap by the loop road. The USFS EDW point (recareaid 67209) plots in the channel about 340 m north-northeast. NHD High Resolution flowline 28 m away. Superseded agency point: USFS EDW Recreation Opportunities, recareaid 67209 'Beasley Flat Picnic Site' (Prescott NF page: 34.47651531, -111.8007081) at 34.476515, -111.800708 (https://apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW/EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01/MapServer/0/query?where=recareaid%3D67209&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=json). Legal boating access: USDA Forest Service, Prescott NF: Beasley Flat Picnic Site; AZ State Parks Paddle Map 2 (Mile 0.0) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/prescott/recreation/beasley-flat-picnic-site): 'It is also the most popular take-out spot for canoes and kayaks after a 10-mile float from White Bridge.' Paddle Map 2: Beasley Flat facilities 'include a concrete boat ramp, a parking lot, toilets'. Spot-check this point first; imagery date is not published by Esri.
